data.reason: Review of attempt 8 (subagent reviewer on opus, triage 127; 126 is an identical duplicate written by accident a moment earlier) passed every criterion and confirmed attempt 7's F1 closed and earlier rounds' findings still closed, but found one medium. F1: _require_the_kill_is_in_the_slice compares killed mutants against the slice's raw names while _require_mutation maps a test to its source first, so a killed-mutant RED is refused for a test-only slice, the very slice the floor refusal tells the author to write. F2 (low): mutation_ci.CONFIG_FILES omits packages/core/tsconfig.json, which the TypeScript checker reads. Ruud decided both are fixed in this ticket (attempt 9). The triage's fingerprint and slice_files failures were judged benign artefacts (only status, ticks and Outcome changed after check 122; every flagged file is named by an earlier accepted plan) and go to harness follow-ups, not this ticket. F1 changes harness/gates.py and F2 harness/mutation_ci.py, which is a new plan, so the return goes to solution.

findings.claim: _require_the_kill_is_in_the_slice compares the killed mutants against the slice's raw file names, but _require_mutation maps a test to its source first; so a RED whose kill is in fee.ts is refused for a slice that names only fee.test.ts.
findings.failure_scenario: SEEN-019's tdd gate refuses fee.ts at 65 with 'Kill the survivors with a test'. The next attempt has one slice naming packages/core/src/fee.test.ts; its RED is a Stryker run, exit 0, mutants_killed {packages/core/src/fee.ts: ['3']}. gates.evaluate refuses: 'every mutant it killed is in a file the slice does not name: killed in packages/core/src/fee.ts, the slice names packages/core/src/fee.test.ts'. The same slice's floor check measures fee.ts. Reproduced by the reviewer with a subclass of AKilledMutantAsRedTest outside the repository.
findings.rule_candidate: none: a mapping mismatch between two gate functions that only a unit test of the killed-mutant citation over a test-only slice can catch

findings.claim: CONFIG_FILES widens to all of src for stryker.config.mjs, vitest.config.ts and package.json, but not for packages/core/tsconfig.json, which the TypeScript checker reads.
findings.failure_scenario: A PR tightens tsconfig.json so a mutant that used to compile becomes a CompileError, or the reverse. CI selects nothing in src, or only the changed files, and Stryker reuses the stored incremental results for unchanged files, which were taken under the old compiler settings.
